messages:
maya_support: Escalation from Acme — embeddings throughput collapsed after yesterday's billing plan change. Customer says API calls return 200 but vectors/sec is ~6x lower while tokens/sec looks normal. They rely on embeddings for realtime similarity; impact is high. Pasting customer notes + sample logs below. Assigning @sasha_eng_ml and @ryan_runtime to investigate.

maya_support: Customer sample (anonymized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxxx' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["...","..."]}'
```
Response headers they observed: `x-vectors-per-request: 2`, `x-model: embed-lite-v1`, `x-request-id: req_ak2j3`
They reported tokens/sec ~= 1.2k but vectors/sec ~= 180 (used to be ~1k). Also some downstream jobs saw `dimension_mismatch` errors when ingesting new vectors into their index.

sasha_eng_ml: Thanks — quick hypotheses: 1) routing fallback to a lower-dim variant (embed-lite) after billing/quota enforcement, 2) client accidentally switched model param, 3) batching behaviour changed causing tiny batches (higher per-vector overhead). Can you share the raw request bodies + a single request id from the time window?

maya_support: Provided req id above `req_ak2j3`. Full request body matches SDK call (they're not overriding model). They said billing UI showed their plan changed at 02:07 UTC (auto-upgrade/downgrade event).

ryan_runtime: I pulled traces for req_ak2j3. Findings:
- routing decision: matched policy `customer_quota_check` -> fallback route `embed-lite-v1` at 02:08:13 UTC
- worker queue depth on embed-service spiked from 3 -> 48 around that time
- avg batch size fell from 8.6 -> 1.3 for the customer namespace
- GPU util for the pool stayed ~65% (no obvious hardware saturation)
- KV-cache miss rate for that namespace jumped 5% -> 62%
So it looks like requests were routed to a different variant which caused downstream adapters to re-encode / re-shape outputs, plus tiny batches causing per-token overhead.

ryan_runtime: Prom queries I used: `sum(rate(embed_requests[5m])) by (route)`, `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(embed_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))`, and `avg_over_time(kvcache_miss_rate[10m])`. I can share graphs in the ticket.

elliot_sre: Any billing events in the infra logs that forced a hard quota? I can see `billing_policy.fallback` events in audit at 02:08:12 for customer org id `org-acme`. That triggered routing to lower-tier variants.

maya_support: Customer confirms they hit a quota enforcement popup and their plan was moved to a trial/downgrade for a billing validation issue. They didn't expect automatic fallback to a lower-dimensional model. They were surprised there was no explicit error or warning in the SDK.

sasha_eng_ml: That explains `dimension_mismatch` errors — downstream indexers expect 1536-d vectors but `embed-lite-v1` returns 512-d. Two vectors outcomes: 1) immediate dimension mismatch errors, 2) silent acceptance + reindexing that slowed throughput.

maya_support: Customer requested repro steps so they can test locally before we apply mitigation.

sasha_eng_ml: Repro steps for support to run:
1) Get a sample request & their API key (use a short-lived test key).
2) Replay sample while forcing the same routing header to simulate fallback: add `-H "X-Redwood-Route: embed-lite-v1"`.
3) Compare headers: `x-model`, `x-vector-dim`, and `x-redirected-by` in the response.
Example:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-test' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -H "X-Redwood-Route: embed-lite-v1" \  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Expected diff: `x-vector-dim: 512` vs normal `1536`.

ryan_runtime: Short-term mitigations:
- Option A: pin model param explicitly to `redwood-embed-1-1536` in customer SDK calls (overrides routing).
- Option B: increase quota/restore plan in billing UI to prevent fallback.
- Option C: route-level hotfix: change billing fallback to return an explicit 402/403 with clear messaging instead of silently routing to a lower-dim model.

maya_support: Customer will accept pinning model as a temporary fix. They've asked us to provide a timeline for permanent change.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `embed-routing-v2` started at 2024-10-18T02:09:00Z — rollout contains new billing fallback behavior (auto-route to embed-lite-v1). Trigger id: canary-9271.

elliot_sre: Action items:
- rollback canary `embed-routing-v2` or change its fallback behavior (ryan).
- coordinate with billing to avoid silent downgrade during validation windows (product + billing).
- add alert: when vectors/sec deviates >30% from tokens/sec for an org for >5m (sasha + runtime).

sasha_eng_ml: Also quick SDK change: if returned `x-vector-dim` != expected, emit a visible warning/error and include `x-redirected-model` header. That will help users detect silent downgrades.

ryan_runtime: I'll patch routing to return 402 + `x-fallback-reason` header for this class of fallback and queue a rollback for the canary. Rolling back now.

maya_support: Thanks all. I'll send the customer a mitigation guide (pin model or restore plan) and an ETA: rollback completed in ~30m, follow-up RCA in a ticket. :thumbsup:

sasha_eng_ml: Nice triage. Long-term: we should decouple billing enforcement from routing decisions. Silent fallback is a reliability footgun.

elliot_sre: Agreed. Logging notes: include route.old_model and route.new_model in routing audit events so support/clients can trace this quickly.

maya_support: I'll close the Slack escalation once the rollback and SDK changes are merged. Will file RCA ticket with links to graphs and the deploy canary id.
